'''GE Healthcare Technologies, Inc.''', stylized '''GE HealthCare''', is an American [[health technology]] company based in [[Chicago]], Illinois. It operates four divisions: [[Medical imaging]], which includes [[molecular imaging]], [[computed tomography]], [[magnetic resonance imaging|magnetic resonance]], [[women’s health]] screening and [[X-ray]] systems; [[Ultrasound]]; Patient Care Solutions, which is focused on [[remote patient monitoring]], [[anesthesia]] and [[respiratory care]], diagnostic [[cardiology]], and infant care; and Pharmaceutical Diagnostics, which manufactures [[contrast agent]]s and [[radiopharmaceutical]]s.<ref name=10K-2024>{{cite web |url=https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/1932393/000193239325000005/gehc-20241231.htm |title=GE Healthcare Technologies Inc. Annual Report (Form 10-K) |date=February 13, 2025 |publisher=[[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]]}}</ref> 

GE HealthCare's primary customers are hospitals and health networks.<ref name=still>{{Cite news | url=https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/this-wide-moat-stock-is-still-buy-even-after-recent-rally | title=This Wide-Moat Stock Is Still a Buy Even After Recent Rally | first=Jay | last=Lee | work=[[Morningstar, Inc.]] | date=September 4, 2024}}</ref> In 2023, the company received 42% of its revenue in the United States and 13% of its revenue from China, where the company faces increasing competition.<ref name=still/>

GE HealthCare was originally the healthcare division of the American conglomerate [[General Electric]] (GE), which [[corporate spin-off|spun it off]] in 2023 as an independent, [[public company|publicly traded]] company. It operates in more than 100 countries, with GE HealthCare major regional operations in Buc (suburb of Paris), France; [[Helsinki]], Finland; [[Kraków]], Poland; [[Budapest]], Hungary; [[Yizhuang, Beijing|Yizhuang]] (suburb of Beijing), China; [[Hino, Tokyo|Hino]] & Tokyo, Japan, and [[Bangalore]], India. Its biggest R&D center is in Bangalore, India, built at a cost of $50 million.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.economist.com/opinion/displaystory.cfm?story_id=15879369 | newspaper=The Economist | title=The world turned upside down | date=15 April 2010}}</ref>

==History==

=== Founding and early growth ===
GE HealthCare traces its roots to the Victor Electric Company, founded in 1893 in a basement by Charles F. Samms and Julius B. Wantz, previously employees of the assembly lines at the Knapp Electrical Works and Midland Electric Co. and then in their early 20s.<ref name="made">{{Cite web |title=Victor X-Ray Corporation, est. 1893 |date=22 September 2015 |url=https://www.madeinchicagomuseum.com/single-post/victor-x-ray-corp/ |publisher=Made In Chicago Museum}}</ref> They initially focused on supplies for the dental industry.<ref name="made" /> At the time, they were a six-person operation.<ref name="made" />

By 1896, one year after [[Wilhelm Röntgen]]'s discovery, Victor Electric entered the business for [[X-ray]] machines. The business expanded rapidly and so, in 1896, the company moved into new premises three times the original size.<ref name="made" /> By 1896, the company also made electrostatic generators for exciting X-ray tubes and electrotherapeutic devices.<ref>{{Citation |title=Victor X-ray Corporation 1893 - 1930 |url=https://collection.sciencemuseumgroup.org.uk/people/cp110613/victor-x-ray-corporation |publisher=[[Science Museum Group]]}}</ref>

By 1903, Victor Electric had outgrown its facilities at 418 Dearborn St. in [[Chicago]] and acquired two floors of a building at 55 Market Street, Chicago.<ref name="made" /> This was again only a temporary stop; by 1910 it was too small and the firm moved again in 1911 to a building at the corner of Jackson Blvd. and Damen Avenue. This was the first permanent home of Victor Electric Co. They stayed there 35 years and during this time, gradually acquired all the space in the building and several around it.

In 1916, the company merged with three companies: Scheidel Western, Snook-Roentgen, MacAlaster & Wiggin.<ref name="made" /> Victor's two founders had key roles in the new firm; Charles F. Samms was company president and Julius B. Wantz was Vice-President of manufacturing and engineering.

=== Acquisition by General Electric ===
In 1920, GE HealthCare entered the imaging technology business with the acquisition of Victor Electric Company, founded in 1893. By 1930 it was renamed to GE X-Ray;<ref name=":3">{{Cite book |last=Donzé |first=Pierre-Yves |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Q2RXEAAAQBAJ |title=Medtech: The Formation and Growth of a Global Industry, 1960–2020 |date=2022-01-01 |publisher=Springer Nature |isbn=978-981-16-7174-6 |language=en}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=78}} Before the introduction of the CT scanner in the 1970s and the MRI scanner in the 1980s, it declined to around 2% of GE's sales among the 120 departments in the conglomerate.<ref name=":3" />{{Reference page|page=78}}

In the 1990s the department began to diversify into various medtech businesses and executed 94 acquisitions between 1995 and 2017.<ref name=":3" />{{Reference page|page=81}} It also continued to invest in research and development, with over 3800 patents between 2000 and 2009.<ref name=":3" />{{Reference page|page=81}}

=== Moving from X-Rays to Medical as GE Medical System ===
Use of X-rays in industry for non-destructive testing of war materials increased during [[World War II]]. X-rays were broadly used as a medical tool for military services.

As the war ended, GE X-Ray Corporation continued to grow. Greater production capacity and greater expertise was needed in the core business of building X-ray tubes. Since the tubes were made from hand-blown glass, the decision was made to move the company 90 miles north to [[Milwaukee]], Wisconsin, in order to tap into the enormous amount of glass-blowing talent in Milwaukee's beer-brewing industry.

In 1947, the company moved from Jackson Blvd. in Chicago to a {{convert|43|acre|m2|adj=on}} site in the city of West Milwaukee, which had been used for building [[turbochargers]] during the war. The street was renamed Electric Avenue.<ref>{{Cite news |date=Sep 16, 2020 |title=GE Healthcare moving jobs to new $50M site in West Milwaukee |url=https://www.wisn.com/article/ge-healthcare-moving-jobs-to-new-dollar50m-site-in-west-milwaukee/34041465 |work=[[WISN-TV]] |location=[[West Milwaukee, Wisconsin]]}}</ref>

In 1951, the corporate structure was dissolved and the name changed to General Electric X-Ray Department. This new name lasted less than 10 years as the department divested itself of its industrial X-ray business, widened its medical business, and took on the name of '''GE Medical Systems Department'''. One of the reasons for the name of Medical Systems was due to the increase in the electro-medical business, which began in 1961 with the introduction of patient monitoring equipment. By 1967 modular equipment was developed which was soon popular in cardiac and intensive care units.

Early in 1960, pacemakers were developed in Corporate Research & Development in [[Schenectady]], New York, and in 1969 the Standby Pacemaker was developed. In 1968, the Biomedical Business Section opened its first factory in Edgerton Avenue. Late in 1970 a surgical package was introduced and in 1971, equipment to monitor blood gasses during surgery was introduced.

Later in 1971, Biomedical opened a 9,000 square meter admin and engineering building opposite its factory and in 1972, the section was renamed The cardio-Surgical Product Section. With the growth of its medical business, the General Electric Company upgraded the department to The Medical Systems Division in 1971. Also in 1971, a major expansion programme was started and the Waukesha factory was planned. Work started in July 1972, and was completed in 1973.

In the 1970s, CT scanners were introduced, followed by MRI machines in the 1980s, and GE became a major manufacturer of both.<ref name=":3" />{{Reference page|page=79}} The department, named GE Medical Systems (GEMS), grew rapidly under the management of [[Jack Welch]], establishing international partnerships and acquisitions.<ref name=":3" />{{Reference page|page=79}} It expanded to sell globally, including various partnerships and acquisitions, growing to 50% sales outside the USA by 1988.<ref name=":3" />{{Reference page|page=79}}

=== Growth in the 1980s as GE Medical Systems ===
In 1982, the company set up a joint venture with [[Yokogawa Electric]]. It changed its name to GE HealthCare Japan Corporation in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=From product sales to solution provider |url=https://www.jetro.go.jp/en/invest/investment_environment/success_stories/gehealthcare.html |publisher=[[Japan External Trade Organization]]}}</ref>

In 1983, GE Medical started investing heavily in [[Magnetic Resonance Imaging]] (MRI) technology, investing nearly US$1 billion in a new plant in [[Waukesha, Wisconsin|Waukesha]]. It developed the MR Signa, which became very successful. Up to this time, the medical Systems Division had simply been divided into domestic and international, but in 1987 it reorganized into the three "poles" of America, Europe and Pacific.

In 1985 GE acquired [[Technicare]] from Johnson and Johnson. Originally named Ohio Nuclear (and in 1979, after another fusion, Ohio Nuclear Unirad), the name was changed to Technicare in 1982. Technicare (with headquarters in Cleveland, Ohio) had been producing a range of rotate-stationary CTs with an installed base in the thousands, as well as some X-ray diagnostic equipment and a nascent [[MRI]] product range.

In 1988, GE Medical Europe merged with CGR (''Compagnie Générale de Radiologie''), a medical equipment supplier based in France, to form General Electric CGR Medical Systems. The European headquarters were moved from [[Hammersmith]] (UK) to [[Buc, Yvelines]], near Paris.

=== Expanding in the 1990s as GE Medical Systems ===
In 1920, Victor was acquired by [[General Electric]] and was renamed VICTOR X-RAY CORPORATION.<ref name="made" /><ref>{{cite journal| journal= Boston Medical and Surgical Journal| title= Announcement of Merging of Victor Electric Corporation with X-Ray interests of General Electric Company| last= Samm| first= C.F.| date= 2 Dec 1920| url=http://booksnow1.scholarsportal.info/ebooks/oca7/34/n23newenglandjour183mass/n23newenglandjour183mass.pdf}}</ref> At that time, it was the largest manufacturer of X-ray tubes.{{citation needed|date=January 2015}}

The merger of the Victor subsidiary and General Electric closed on July 28, 1926 and the company became "General Electric X-Ray Corporation".<ref name="made" /> The merger brought renewed vitality to the organization and Victor entered the foreign market with equipment sold and serviced in nearly 70 countries. In 1930, the Victor name was phased-out from all branding; however, advertisements did mention "formerly Victor X-Ray Corporation".<ref name="made" />

In 1974, work on [[Computed tomography|CT]] was started and the first CT machine was installed in 1976. In June 1980, the company acquired the CT scanner business of [[EMI]].<ref>{{Cite journal | title=GE buys EMI CT scanner business | first=E | last=Kuntz | journal=Modern Healthcare | publisher=[[National Institutes of Health]] | date=June 1980| volume=10 | issue=6 | page=12 | pmid=10247365 }}</ref>

[[File:MRI Scanner at Narayana Multispeciality Hospital, Jaipur.jpg|alt=GE Signa series MRI Scanner, used at Narayana Multispeciality Hospital, Jaipur|thumb|GE Signa series MRI Scanner, used at Narayana Multispeciality Hospital, Jaipur]]The MRI magnet plant in [[Florence, South Carolina]], was opened a short time later, giving GE its own magnet production. It underwent a $40 million expansion in 2017.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://scnow.com/news/officials-weigh-in-on-ge-healthcare-s-40-million-expansion-in-florence-county/article_b9ca0266-0e4e-11e7-b377-f3d8a1e3b4f0.html | title=Officials weigh in on GE Healthcare's $40 million expansion | work=[[The Morning News (American newspaper)|The Morning News]] | date=March 21, 2017 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

GE HealthCare was incorporated in 1994.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://appext20.dos.ny.gov/corp_public/CORPSEARCH.SELECT_ENTITY |title=GE HEALTHCARE INC. |publisher=New York State Department of State Division of Corporations}}</ref>

In 1992, GE acquired the Picker Service organization in the U.K.

In 1994, it changed the name in Europe from GE-CGR back to General Electric Medical Systems.

In September 1995, the company acquired Resonex, an MRI maker based in [[Fremont, California]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/63293-77#overview |title=Resonex Overview | publisher=Pitchbook}}</ref>

In 1996, Jeff Immelt was named CEO of the company; he became CEO of GE in 2000.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://money.cnn.com/2000/11/27/companies/immelt/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030219044536/http://money.cnn.com/2000/11/27/companies/immelt/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=February 19, 2003 | title=Immelt, the man for GE | work=[[CNN]] | date=November 27, 2000}}</ref>

In April 1998, the company acquired Diasonics Vingmed from [[Elbit Medical Imaging]] of [[Haifa]], Israel, expanding its ultrasound imaging business.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/milwaukee/stories/1998/04/06/daily12.html |title=GE Medical acquires Diasonics Vingmed | work=[[American City Business Journals]] |date=April 9, 1998 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In September 1998, the company acquired Marquette Medical Systems for $808 million.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-sep-22-fi-25150-story.html | title=GE Medical Agrees to Buy Marquette for $808 Million | work=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=September 22, 1998 | url-access=limited}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB906385745621036500 | title=General Electric Unit to Acquire Marquette Medical for $824 Million | first=Ron | last=Winslow | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=September 22, 1998 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://money.cnn.com/1998/09/21/deals/marquette/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020213005617/http://money.cnn.com/1998/09/21/deals/marquette/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=February 13, 2002 | title=GE improves its imaging | work=[[CNN]] | date=September 21, 1998}}</ref>

In November 1998, the company acquired the Nuclear and MR businesses of [[Elscint]], (then a division of [[Elron Electronic Industries|Elron]], based in Haifa, Israel), for $100 million.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/11/19/business/company-news-elscint-to-sell-unit-to-ge-medical-for-100-million.html | title=Elscint to Sell Unit to GE Medical for $100 million | agency=[[Bloomberg News]] | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=November 19, 1998 | url-access=limited}}</ref>

===21st century and renaming to GE HealthCare===

==== 2000–2005 ====
In September 2000, the company acquired the remaining 50% of the ELGEMS joint-venture formed with Elscint in 1997.<ref>{{cite news |date=September 13, 2000 |title=GE to acquire Elscint's share in ELGEMS |url=https://www.diagnosticimaging.com/view/ge-acquire-elscints-share-elgems |work=Diagnostic Imaging}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=January 4, 2001 |title=GE buys out Elscint's 50% of joint venture ELGEMS for $30 millipon |url=https://www.thestreet.com/technology/ge-buys-out-elscints-50-of-joint-venture-elgems-for-30-millipon-1239212 |work=[[TheStreet.com]]}}</ref>

In 2001, the company acquired San Francisco, California–based CT maker Imatron for $210 million. Imatron produced an [[Electron beam tomography]] (EBT) scanner that performs imaging applications used by physicians specializing in cardiology, pulmonology and gastroenterology. The Imatron business was later incorporated into GE HealthCare's Diagnostic Imaging business segment.

In March 2002, the company acquired MedicaLogic, creator of the former ''Logician'', an ambulatory [[Electronic Medical Records]] system, for approximately $32 million.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/portland/stories/2002/03/18/daily18.html | title=GE Medical to pay $35.2M for MedicaLogic health-record assets | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=March 19, 2002 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In April 2002, GE HealthCare acquired Visualization Technology, a manufacturer of intra-operative medical devices and related products for use in minimally invasive image guided surgery, based in Boston.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.photonics.com/Articles/GE_Medical_Systems_To_Acquire_Visualization/a11897 | title=GE Medical Systems To Acquire Visualization Technology | work=Photonics.com | date=February 15, 2002}}</ref>

In January 2003, the company acquired Millbrook Corporation, maker of Millbrook Practice Manager, a billing and scheduling system for doctors' offices.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.modernhealthcare.com/article/20030101/MODERNPHYSICIAN/301010710/ge-medical-snaps-up-millbrook | title=GE Medical snaps up Millbrook | first=Neil | last=Versel | work=[[Modern Healthcare]] | date=December 31, 2002}}</ref>

GE HealthCare IT later merged the two products into one, although the stand-alone EMR product is still available and in development.

In 2003, GE HealthCare acquired Instrumentarium, including its Datex-Ohmeda division, a producer, manufacturer, and supplier of anesthesia machines and mechanical ventilators. To satisfy regulatory concerns in the United States and in Europe, GE HealthCare was forced to divest Instrumentarium's Ziehm Imaging [[mobile C-arm]] business, as well as its Spacelabs patient-monitoring unit.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna3130384 | title=GE clinches Instrumentarium deal | agency=[[Reuters]] | work=[[NBC News]] | date=October 6, 2003}}</ref>

[[File:GE Healthcare Amersham radiopharmaceuticals packaging.jpg|thumb|Packaging radioactive pharmaceuticals at GE Healthcare's facility in [[Amersham]], England]]

In April 2004, the company acquired [[Amersham plc]].<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2003/oct/11/1 | title=Amersham agrees to £5.7bn GE takeover | first=David | last=Gow | work=[[The Guardian]] | date=11 October 2003}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB106574018488408500 | title=GE Unveils $9.5 Billion Deal To Acquire U.K.'s Amersham | first1=Anita | last1=Raghavan | first2=Kathryn | last2=Kranhold | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=October 10, 2003 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Also in 2004, GE HealthCare along with other healthcare companies built a research reactor for neutron and unit cell research at GE's European Research Center near [[Garching]] (outside of [[Munich]]), Germany. It is the only such reactor currently in operation.

==== 2006–2014 ====
In 2006, [[Sir William Castell]] resigned as CEO to become Chairman of the [[Wellcome Trust]], a charity that fosters and promotes human and animal research—in the United Kingdom. Former GE Medical Systems CEO Joe Hogan then became CEO.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/06/24/business/ge-realigns-its-11-businesses-into-6-and-shuffles-executives.html | title=G.E. Realigns Its 11 Businesses Into 6 and Shuffles Executives | first=Jeff | last=Bailey | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=June 24, 2005 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In January 2006, the company acquired [[IDX Systems Corporation]] for $1.2 billion. IDX was folded into GE HealthCare Integrated IT Solutions, which specializes in clinical information systems and healthcare revenue management.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB112799698824455643 | title=GE Agrees to Acquire IDX Systems, Boosting Portfolio in Health-Care IT | first=Kathryn | last=Kranhold | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=September 30, 2005 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.rutlandherald.com/news/ge-to-acquire-idx-in-1-2-billion-deal/article_9f385925-59a4-5dc4-a045-f3bb3def2404.html | title=GE to acquire IDX in $1.2 billion deal | first=ROSS | last=SNEYD | agency=[[Associated Press]] | work=[[Rutland Herald]] | date=September 30, 2005}}</ref>

January 2007, The U.S. Food and Drug Administration stopped GE OEC the Salt Lake-based design and manufacturing plant from selling its surgical imaging systems stating that the OEC systems could put patients at risk.[27]

In February 2008, GE HealthCare acquired [[Whatman plc]], a global supplier of filtration products and technologies for £363 million.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.genomeweb.com/archive/ge-healthcare-acquire-whatman-713m | title=GE Healthcare to Acquire Whatman for $713M | work=[[GenomeWeb]] | date=February 4, 2008 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In July 2008, Joseph Hogan announced his intent to leave his post as CEO of GE HealthCare to take the role of CEO at [[ABB Asea Brown Boveri|ABB]]. John Dineen, head of GE's Transportation division since 2005, was named CEO.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://instrumentbusinessoutlook.com/press-release/john-dineen-named-president-and-ceo-of-ge-healthcare-lorenzo-simonelli-to-lead-ge-transportation/ | title=John Dineen Named President and CEO of GE Healthcare; Lorenzo Simonelli to Lead GE Transportation | work=Instrument Business Outlook | date=July 17, 2008}}</ref>

In March 2010, the company acquired MedPlexus.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.modernhealthcare.com/article/20100324/NEWS/303249954/ge-healthcare-makes-deal-for-medplexus | title=GE Healthcare makes deal for MedPlexus | first=Maureen | last=McKinney | work=[[Modern Healthcare]] | date=March 24, 2010 | url-access=subscription}}</ref> The company then offered its first electronic medical record product in a software-as-a-service platform.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/article/world/ge-offers-e-health-records-as-saas-offering-idUS255680050/ | title=GE offers e-health records as SaaS offering | work=[[Reuters]] | date=June 16, 2010}}</ref>

In April 2010, the company announced it was investing €3 million in the Technology Research for Independent Living Centre. The Irish centre seeks to enhance independence for elderly people through technological innovation.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.mobihealthnews.com/7489/ge-invests-3m-in-independent-living-center | title=GE invests $3M in independent living center | first=Brian | last=Dolan | work=MobiHealth ENews | date=May 4, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://sciencebusiness.net/news/68209/GE-Healthcare-puts-%243-million-into-TRIL-Centre-for-independent-living-technologies |title=GE Healthcare puts $3 million into TRIL Centre for independent living technologies | work=Science Business | date=28 April 2010}}</ref>

==== 2015–2020 ====
In July 2015, GE HealthCare partnered with the 2015 [[CrossFit Games]] to provide athletes with [[mobile imaging]] equipment.<ref>{{cite press release | url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20150720005125/en/GE-to-Provide-Mobile-Imaging-Equipment-for-Athletes-at-2015-REEBOK-CROSSFIT-GAMES | title=GE to Provide Mobile Imaging Equipment for Athletes at 2015 Reebok Crossfit Games | publisher=[[Business Wire]] | date=July 20, 2015}}</ref>

The following year in January 2016, the company announced the move of its global headquarters to [[Chicago]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2016/01/11/ge-healthcare-moving-headquarters-to-chicago-from-uk/ |title=GE Healthcare moving headquarters to Chicago from U.K. |last=Janssen |first=Kim |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] | date=January 11, 2016 | url-access=limited}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/ge-healthcare-moving-headquarters-to-chicago/2002050/ |title=GE Healthcare Moving Global Headquarters to Chicago |first=Justin | last=Ray | work=[[NBC Chicago]] | date=January 11, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.chicagobusiness.com/article/20160111/BLOGS02/160119985/ge-healthcare-moving-headquarters-to-chicago | title=Chicago snares another corporate HQ | work=[[Crain Communications]] | date=January 11, 2016}}</ref>

In June 2017, Kieran Murphy was named CEO of the company, and former CEO [[John L. Flannery]] was named CEO of GE.<ref>{{Cite press release |url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20170612005521/en/Kieran-Murphy-Appointed-CEO-GE-Healthcare-Succeeding |title=Kieran Murphy Appointed CEO of GE Healthcare, Succeeding John Flannery | publisher=[[Business Wire]] |date=June 12, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/milwaukee/news/2017/06/13/ge-healthcares-new-ceo-murphy-has-been-leading.html | title=GE Healthcare's new CEO Murphy has been leading Massachusetts-based division | first=Jessica | last=Bartlett | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=June 13, 2017 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In April 2018, GE HealthCare sold several healthcare information technology assets to [[Veritas Capital]] for $1.05 billion.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-04-02/ge-to-sell-health-it-assets-in-1-billion-private-equity-deal | title=GE to Sell Health IT Assets to Veritas in $1.05 Billion Deal |last=Clough |first=Rick |work=[[Bloomberg News]] | date=April 2, 2018 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In June 2018, GE first announced plans to spin off GE HealthCare.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/milwaukee/news/2018/06/26/major-area-employer-ge-healthcare-to-be-spun-off.html | title=Major area employer GE Healthcare to be spun off as stand-alone company |last=Kirchen |first=Rich | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=June 26, 2018 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2018/06/26/general-electric-healthcare-baker-hughes/733611002/ | title=General Electric to spin off GE Healthcare, offload Baker Hughes oilfield services |last=Bomey |first=Nathan | work=[[USA TODAY]] | date=June 26, 2018}}</ref> However, the plan was delayed after GE sold its biopharma business to [[Danaher Corporation]] for $21.4 billion.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/02/25/ge-withdraws-plans-for-healthcare-ipo-after-danaher-deal-bloomberg.html |title=GE Healthcare IPO this year 'looks unlikely' after Danaher deal, CEO Culp says |last=Sheetz | first=Michael |work=[[CNBC]] |date=25 February 2019}}</ref>

==== 2021–2025 ====
In January 2021, the company acquired Prismatic Sensors AB, focused on Deep Silicon detector technology.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.biospace.com/ge-healthcare-pioneers-photon-counting-ct-with-prismatic-sensors-acquisition?s=79 | title=GE Healthcare Pioneers Photon Counting CT with Prismatic Sensors Acquisition | work=Biospace | date=November 20, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.kth.se/sci/nyheter/ge-buys-swedish-start-up-prismatic-sensors-1.1039760 | title=GE buys Swedish start-up Prismatic Sensors | first=Mats | last=Danielsson | work=[[KTH Royal Institute of Technology]] | date=January 4, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite press release | url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20201120005166/en/GE-Healthcare-Pioneers-Photon-Counting-CT-with-Prismatic-Sensors-Acquisition | title=GE Healthcare Pioneers Photon Counting CT with Prismatic Sensors Acquisition | publisher=[[Business Wire]] | date=November 20, 2020}}</ref> A few months later in May 2021, the company acquired Zionexa, a company focused on [[biomarker]]s for the detection of [[breast cancer]].<ref>{{Cite press release | url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210506005720/en/GE-Healthcare-Acquires-Zionexa-Molecular-Imaging-Agent-Aims-to-Enable-More-Targeted-Treatment-for-Metastatic-Breast-Cancer-Patients | title=GE Healthcare Acquires Zionexa; Molecular Imaging Agent Aims to Enable More Targeted Treatment for Metastatic Breast Cancer Patients | publisher=[[Business Wire]] | date=May 6, 2021}}</ref>

In July 2021, the company integrated technology from Spectronic Medical to create [[artificial intelligence]]-based software.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://g-medtech.com/news/jp/ge-healthcare-to-offer-end-to-end-deep-learning-solutions-with-spectronic-medical-to-improve-accuracy-for-radiation-oncology-treatment/ | title=GE Healthcare to Offer End-To-End Deep Learning Solutions with Spectronic Medical to Improve Accuracy for Radiation Oncology Treatment | date=July 9, 2021}}</ref>

In November 2021, [[General Electric]] announced it would split into three publicly traded companies, with GE HealthCare being one of the three.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/ge-puts-31-billion-value-on-spinoff-of-ge-healthcare-technologies-11669847256 |title=General Electric Sets Healthcare Division Spinoff Plans |last=Gryta |first=Thomas | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=November 30, 2022 | url-access=subscription}}</ref> The spin-off of GE HealthCare was completed on January 4, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=HealthCare; Confirms Target Spin-Off Timing of First Week of January 2023 |url=https://www.ge.com/news/press-releases/ge-announces-board-of-directors-for-future-independent-ge-healthcare-confirms-target |website=www.ge.com |publisher=GE News}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/ge-health-care-begins-trading-as-spin-off-heralds-shift-to-corporate-streamlining-194525168.html | title=GE HealthCare begins trading as spin-off heralds shift to corporate streamlining | last=Juang | first=Mike | work=[[Yahoo! Finance]] | date=January 4, 2023 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105000237/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/ge-health-care-begins-trading-as-spin-off-heralds-shift-to-corporate-streamlining-194525168.html | archivedate=January 5, 2023 | url-status=live}}</ref> Prior to the spin-off, the company acquired BK Medical from Altaris Capital Partners for $1.45 billion.<ref>{{cite press release | url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20211221005455/en/GE-Healthcare-Completes-Acquisition-of-BK-Medical | title=GE Healthcare Completes Acquisition of BK Medical | publisher=[[Business Wire]] | date=December 21, 2021}}</ref>

Following its separation, GE HealthCare continued to expand. In February 2023, the company acquired Caption Health, an [[artificial intelligence]] medical technology manufacturer headquartered in [[San Mateo, California]], for $150 million.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/GE-HEALTHCARE-TECHNOLOGIE-148175835/news/GE-HealthCare-Technologies-Inc-completed-the-acquisition-of-Caption-Health-Inc-43660614/ | title=GE HealthCare Technologies Inc. completed the acquisition of Caption Health, Inc. | work=Market Screener | date=February 16, 2023}}</ref>

In July 2024, the company acquired the clinical [[artificial intelligence]] business from Intelligent Ultrasound for $51 million.<ref>{{Cite press release | url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240717580041/en/GE-HealthCare-announces-agreement-to-acquire-clinical-artificial-intelligence-business-from-Intelligent-Ultrasound | title=GE HealthCare announces agreement to acquire clinical artificial intelligence business from Intelligent Ultrasound | publisher=[[Business Wire]] | date=July 18, 2024}}</ref>

In March 2025, GE HealthCare introduced the Freelium sealed magnet platform for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The system uses less than 1% of the helium required by traditional imaging systems, and is intended to support more sustainable imaging and improve access to imaging in regions with limited helium supply.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/ge-healthcare-mr-freelium-technology-2016-11|title=A new technology is being developed using just 1% of the finite resource needed for traditional MRIs|date=Nov 29, 2016|access-date=Nov 28, 2025|website=Business Insider|last=Pflanzer|first=Lydia Ramsey}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/gehc-stock-may-rise-freelium-magnet-launch-boosts-mr-access|title=GEHC Stock May Rise on Freelium Magnet Launch, Boosts MR Access|date=March 3, 2025|access-date=Nov 28, 2025|website=Nasdaq}}</ref>

In April 2025, GE HealthCare entered a partnership with FPT. A few months later they established a multi-year collaboration with Ascension, a non-profit health system. The two companies plan to work together to improve Ascension's patient access, safety, and care quality.<ref>{{Cite web|title=GE HealthCare and Ascension Form Multi-Year Technology Partnership {{!}} The Healthcare Technology Report.|url=https://thehealthcaretechnologyreport.com/ge-healthcare-and-ascension-form-multi-year-technology-partnership/|access-date=2025-11-29|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=GE HealthCare signs partnership with Vietnamese IT company FPT|url=https://www.consultancy.asia/news/6011/ge-healthcare-signs-partnership-with-vietnamese-it-company-fpt|website=www.consultancy.asia|date=2025-04-03|access-date=2025-11-29|language=en}}</ref>

In November 2025, the company entered an agreement to acquire Intelerad Medical Systems for $2.3 billion.<ref>{{Cite press release | url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251120042915/en/GE-HealthCare-to-acquire-Intelerad-advancing-cloud-enabled-enterprise-imaging-across-care-settings | title=GE HealthCare to acquire Intelerad, advancing cloud-enabled enterprise imaging across care settings | publisher=[[Business Wire]] | date=November 20, 2025}}</ref>

== Business overview ==
For 2024, the company reported nearly $20 billion in total revenue split between about $13 billion in products and about $6.6 billion in services, growing by 2% from the prior year.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=GE HealthCare reports fourth quarter and full year 2024 financial results |url=https://investor.gehealthcare.com/news-releases/news-release-details/ge-healthcare-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024}}</ref>

As of 2025, the company reports its revenue broken down into four [[Market segmentation|segments]] in accordance with the segment reporting accounting requirements (ASU 2023-07):

# Imaging, which accounted for about $2.4 billion in 2024Q4<ref name=":0" />
# Advanced Visualization Solutions, with $1.4 billion in 2024Q4
# Patient Care Solutions, with $827 million in 2024Q4
# Pharmaceutical Diagnostics with $646 million 2024Q4
Major competitors include [[Fujifilm]], [[Siemens Healthineers]], and other companies in the [[Medical imaging#Industry|medical imaging industry]].

=== Imaging ===
The imaging business was the original core starting with x-rays in 1920, CT scanners in the 1970s, and MRI machines in the 1980s.<ref name=":3" />{{Reference page|page=79}}

As of 2024, it includes the original imaging businesses along with continued innovations, such as the digital Omni Legend PET/CT scanner introduced in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=vasundhara |date=2022-10-17 |title=GE Healthcare launches Omni Legend digital PET/CT System |url=https://www.medicaldevice-network.com/news/ge-healthcare-omni-legend/ |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=Medical Device Network |language=en-US}}</ref>

GE uses a custom scientific [[Linux]] distribution HELiOS (Healthcare Enterprise Linux Operating System) on their machines.<ref>{{Cite web |last=leah |date=2017-02-20 |title=Scientific Linux: Created for physics, now used in medicine |url=https://news.fnal.gov/2017/02/scientific-linux-created-physics-now-used-medicine |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=News |language=en-US}}</ref> They partnered with [[SUSE S.A.|SUSE]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Converting from HELiOS to SLES: The GE Healthcare experience. |url=https://www.suse.com/susecon/archive/?year=2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250727000000/https://www.suse.com/susecon/archive/?year=2020 |archive-date=2025-07-27 |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=www.suse.com |series=CAS-1274 |language=en}} [https://links.imagerelay.com/cdn/3404/ql/42ed92559c0a4e6992b7c61364daa9eb/CAS-1274-SD20_Converting_from_HELiOS_to_SLES_The_GE_Healthcare_experience.pdf Alt URL]</ref>

== Facilities ==
The company's headquarters are in Chicago on the sixteenth floor of the [[Heller International Building]]. In 2019, it consolidated hundreds of employees, particularly in technology, from [[Barrington, Illinois]] to its Chicago headquarters.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Graham |first=Meg |date=2017-02-23 |title=GE Healthcare moving hundreds of jobs from Barrington to Chicago |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2017/02/23/ge-healthcare-moving-hundreds-of-jobs-from-barrington-to-chicago/ |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2020, it relocated salespeople to the headquarters from Wisconsin or regional sales offices countrywide.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Boulton |first=Guy |title=GE Healthcare would invest $50 million in a new factory in West Milwaukee under proposed plan |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/money/business/health-care/2020/09/16/ge-healthcare-invest-50-million-new-factory-west-milwaukee/5817282002/ |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=Journal Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref>

The company has a major presence in [[Waukesha, Wisconsin]], where as of 2023 over half of its 5200 Wisconsin employees were located.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Schulz |first=Joe |date=2023-11-17 |title=GE HealthCare to consolidate Milwaukee and Wauwatosa operations in Waukesha |url=https://www.wpr.org/economy/ge-healthcare-consolidate-milwaukee-and-wauwatosa-operations-waukesha |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=WPR |language=en-US}}</ref> The company collaborates with researchers at [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]] which is less than 80 miles away.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-05-11 |title=GE Healthcare, UW partnership sharpens medical imaging advances |url=http://wisconsinidea.wisc.edu/features/charles-mistretta-ge-healthcare-uw-partnership-sharpens-medical-imaging-advances/ |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=News |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Manufacturing factories ===
As of 2024, around two-thirds of CT scanners are produced in China, particularly in the [[Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area]] where GE launched its first joint venture, GE Hangwei Medical Systems, Co., Ltd., in China in 1991.<ref>{{Cite web |title=China's opening up brings broad opportunities for multinational corporations - People's Daily Online |url=https://en.people.cn/n3/2024/0805/c90000-20202143.html |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=en.people.cn}}</ref> GE also has a manufacturing facility in India, which launched in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=GE Healthcare Boosts Local Manufacturing In India, New Factory Goes Live |url=https://www.gehealthcare.in/about/newsroom/press-releases/ge-healthcare-boosts-local-manufacturing-in-india-new-factory-goes-live?npclid=botnpclid |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=www.gehealthcare.in}}</ref>

As of 2023, the company has a manufacturing plant in 4855 W. Electric Ave., [[West Milwaukee, Wisconsin|West Milwaukee]] which produces imaging tubes and detectors.<ref name=":1" /> It announced plans to expand the plant in 2020 to produce more components for PET and CT scanners.<ref name=":2" /> The company began its presence in the region in 1947 during a post-World War II shift by GE X-Ray.<ref>{{Cite web |title=GE Healthcare |url=https://emke.uwm.edu/entry/ge-healthcare/ |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=Encyclopedia of Milwaukee |language=en-US}}</ref>

The company has a plant in [[North Aurora, Illinois]]; in 2025, workers there voted to join the [[International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers]] (IAM), which also represents workers in [[Warrensville Heights, Ohio]] and Wisconsin.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allard |first=Sam |date=2025-01-16 |title=Workers unionize at Aurora GE Healthcare facility |url=https://www.axios.com/local/cleveland/2025/01/16/aurora-ge-healthcare-labor-union-iam |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref>

In 2009, a new 230k square foot plant in [[Troy, New York]] was completed for manufacturing digital mammography x-ray machines,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-09-10 |title=New product lines help GE Healthcare workforce grow |url=https://www.benningtonbanner.com/local-news/new-product-lines-help-ge-healthcare-workforce-grow/article_b2e2cf6e-603c-5b8f-81c1-7dd8c636f758.html |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=Bennington Banner |language=en}}</ref> incorporating digital flat panel X-ray technology using research conducted in [[Niskayuna, New York]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=GE Healthcare opens $165M production facility in N.Y. |url=https://www.reliableplant.com/Read/18055/ge-healthcare-opens-$165m-production-facility-in-ny |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=www.reliableplant.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Criticism==
=== Gadolinium-based contrast agents ===
In 1994, GE HealthCare ignored advice of its safety experts to proactively restrict the use of its [[MRI contrast agent]], Omniscan.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.propublica.org/article/ges-own-safety-team-urged-company-to-restrict-mri-drug-041510 | title=GE's Own Safety Team Urged Company to Restrict MRI Drug |last=Gerth | first=Jeff | work=[[ProPublica]] |date=April 15, 2010}}</ref> It also tried to conceal evidence of its risks by allegedly telling a researcher to "burn the data", as revealed during a trial opposing debilitated consumers, due to its accumulation in multiple organs. This allegation was denied by GE HealthCare.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gerth |first=Jeff |date=March 7, 2013 |title='Burn the Data': Did a Company Try to Hide Risks of MRI Dye Omniscan? |url=https://www.propublica.org/article/burn-the-data-did-a-company-try-to-hide-risks-of-ges-mri-dye |work=[[ProPublica]]}}</ref>

In 2009, GE HealthCare sued for defamation by a radiologist at the University of Copenhagen Hospital who linked the uses of Omniscan to [[Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis|gadolinium induced fibrosis]] after twenty of his patients (from which 1 died) suffered from it after its administration.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.propublica.org/article/ges-omniscan-lawsuit-ratchets-up-volume-in-british-libel-debate-1219 | title=GE Suit Hushes Scientist Critical of Omniscan |last=Gerth |first=Jeff | work=[[ProPublica]] | date=December 19, 2009}}</ref>

In 2017, GE HealthCare opposed the [[European Medicines Agency]] (EMA) suspending the use of Omniscan (along with other linear agents), despite evidence of the high [[cytotoxicity]] of gadodiamide<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bower |first1=Danielle V. |last2=Richter | first2=Johannes K. |last3=von Tengg-Kobligk |first3=Hendrik |last4=Heverhagen | first4=Johannes T. |last5=Runge |first5=Val M. |date=August 2019 |title=Gadolinium-Based MRI Contrast Agents Induce Mitochondrial Toxicity and Cell Death in Human Neurons, and Toxicity Increases With Reduced Kinetic Stability of the Agent | url=https://boris.unibe.ch/132314/1/Gad_Bower.pdf|journal=Investigative Radiology | volume=54 |issue=8 |pages=453–463|doi=10.1097/RLI.0000000000000567 |issn=1536-0210 |pmid=31265439 |s2cid=164486744}}</ref> and its likelihood to dissociate after deposition. GE HealthCare said at the time it believed the overall benefit-risk profile of linear agents including Omniscan was positive and should remain as an option for radiologists.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-03-16 |title=GE Health asks EMA to reconsider proposal to stop sale of MRI drug |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/ge-health-asks-ema-reconsider-proposal-stop-sale-202221489--sector.html |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=Reuters via Yahoo News |language=en-US}}</ref>

In a 2020 study, four commercially available gadolinium-based MRI contrast agents were tested: gadoteridol (ProHance), gadoterate (Dotarem, Clariscan) and gadobutrol (Gadovist). Of the four, gadoteridol demonstrated the lowest levels of retained gadolinium in the brain and soft body tissues of the rats used for the study. None of the tested agents had any impact on kidney histology.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bussi |first1=Simona |last2=Coppo |first2=Alessandra |last3=Celeste |first3=Roberto |last4=Fanizzi |first4=Antonello |last5=Fringuello Mingo |first5=Alberto |last6=Ferraris |first6=Andrea |last7=Botteron |first7=Catherine |last8=Kirchin |first8=Miles A. |last9=Tedoldi |first9=Fabio |last10=Maisano |first10=Federico |date=2020-02-04 |title=Macrocyclic MR contrast agents: evaluation of multiple-organ gadolinium retention in healthy rats |journal=Insights into Imaging |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=11 |doi=10.1186/s13244-019-0824-5 |doi-access=free |issn=1869-4101 |pmc=7000570 |pmid=32020385}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bussi|first1=Simona|last2=Coppo|first2=Alessandra|last3=Celeste|first3=Roberto|last4=Fanizzi |first4=Antonello |last5=Fringuello Mingo|first5=Alberto|last6=Ferraris |first6=Andrea |last7=Botteron |first7=Catherine|last8=Kirchin|first8=Miles A.|last9=Tedoldi |first9=Fabio |last10=Maisano|first10=Federico |date=2020-02-04|title=Macrocyclic MR contrast agents: evaluation of multiple-organ gadolinium retention in healthy rats|journal=Insights into Imaging |volume=11|issue=1|page=11|doi=10.1186/s13244-019-0824-5 |issn=1869-4101 |pmc=7000570 |pmid=32020385 |doi-access=free }}</ref> However, a separate 2022 study where rats were administered eighty human equivalent doses of various gadolinium-based contrast agents demonstrated that gadoterate had the lowest levels of gadolinium detected in specific areas of the brain and kidneys. Additionally, behavioral studies have been shown that there are no effects on any neurological parameters.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ayers-Ringler |first1=Jennifer |last2=McDonald |first2=Jennifer S. |last3=Connors |first3=Margaret A. |last4=Fisher |first4=Cody R. |last5=Han |first5=Susie |last6=Jakaitis |first6=Daniel R. |last7=Scherer |first7=Bradley |last8=Tutor |first8=Gabriel |last9=Wininger |first9=Katheryn M. |last10=Dai |first10=Daying |last11=Choi |first11=Doo-Sup |last12=Salisbury |first12=Jeffrey L. |last13=Jannetto |first13=Paul J. |last14=Bornhorst |first14=Joshua A. |last15=Kadirvel |first15=Ram |date=March 2022 |title=Neurologic Effects of Gadolinium Retention in the Brain after Gadolinium-based Contrast Agent Administration |journal=Radiology |volume=302 |issue=3 |pages=676–683 |doi=10.1148/radiol.210559 |issn=0033-8419 |pmc=8893178 |pmid=34931861}}</ref>

===Low taxes paid in the United Kingdom===
According to a report in ''[[The Independent]]'' in January 2016, the company received more money back in tax benefits (£1.6 million) in the UK in the previous 12 years than it paid. Its UK operations are all ultimately owned by a holding company in the Netherlands. Tax paid was £250,000, 1.7% of its £14.3 million profit. The company employs 22,000 people in the UK.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/health/ge-healthcare-us-healthcare-giant-makes-fortune-from-nhs-but-pays-hardly-a-penny-in-tax/34389998.html |title=GE Healthcare: US healthcare giant makes fortune from NHS but pays hardly a penny in tax | work=[[Belfast Telegraph]] |date=23 January 2016}}</ref>

===Overbilling the government===
In 2011, the company agreed to pay $30 million to settle allegations that a company it acquired in 2004, Amersham Health, violated the [[False Claims Act of 1863]] by knowingly providing false or misleading information to [[Medicare (United States)|Medicare]], causing the government to reimburse [[Myoview]] at artificially inflated rates. By maximizing the number of times a vial of the solution was used, health care providers billed Medicare multiple times for the product. A [[whistleblower]] received $5.1 million in the settlement.<ref name=":4">{{Cite press release | url=https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/ge-healthcare-inc-pays-us-30-million-resolve-false-claims-act-allegations | title=GE Healthcare Inc. Pays U.S. $30 Million to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations | publisher=[[United States Department of Justice]] | date=December 29, 2011}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite news | url=https://abcnews.go.com/Business/ge-healthcare-agrees-30-million-settlement/story?id=15253667 | title=GE Healthcare agrees to $30 million settlement | work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] | date=December 29, 2011}}</ref> GE admitted no wrongdoing in the settlement, noting that the allegations pertain to over a year before it acquired Nycomed Amersham.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" />

===Reliability of imaging system===
The company supplies a cloud-based imaging system to the East Midlands Radiology Consortium, which was described in October 2017 as breaking down, so that medical images had to be sent between hospitals by taxi.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.hsj.co.uk/technology-and-innovation/patient-images-sent-by-taxi-after-30m-it-system-breaks-down/7020755.article | title=Patient images sent by taxi after £30m IT system breaks down | first=Shaun | last=Lintern | work=[[Health Service Journal]] |date=11 October 2017}}</ref>

GE Healthcare Technologies, Inc., stylized GE HealthCare, is an American health technology company based in Chicago, Illinois. It operates four divisions: Medical imaging, which includes molecular imaging, computed tomography, magnetic resonance, women’s health screening and X-ray systems; Ultrasound; Patient Care Solutions, which is focused on remote patient monitoring, anesthesia and respiratory care, diagnostic cardiology, and infant care; and Pharmaceutical Diagnostics, which manufactures contrast agents and radiopharmaceuticals. 
GE HealthCare's primary customers are hospitals and health networks. In 2023, the company received 42% of its revenue in the United States and 13% of its revenue from China, where the company faces increasing competition.
GE HealthCare was originally the healthcare division of the American conglomerate General Electric (GE), which spun it off in 2023 as an independent, publicly traded company. It operates in more than 100 countries, with GE HealthCare major regional operations in Buc (suburb of Paris), France; Helsinki, Finland; Kraków, Poland; Budapest, Hungary; Yizhuang (suburb of Beijing), China; Hino & Tokyo, Japan, and Bangalore, India. Its biggest R&D center is in Bangalore, India, built at a cost of $50 million.
